nodes.summary: The unordered pairs of positions `i < j` among `k` blocks.
nodes.title: Unordered pairs of blocks

nodes.summary: The random-joining law has finite support, and the expectation of a statistic of the `j`-th visited list (`j ≤ m`) is the `j`-th iterate of `joinStep`.
nodes.title: Random joining has finite support and iterates the join step

nodes.summary: Expected site frequency spectrum (Fu 1995). Let the genealogy of a sample of `n` gene copies consist of Kingman holding times `K.T` and an independent block-size history `τ` with the random-joining law. If, given the genealogy (the σ-algebra generated by `τ` and the holding times), the number `ξ i` of sites whose derived allele is carried by exactly `i` copies is integrable and has conditional mean `(θ / 2) L_i`…
nodes.title: Expected site frequency spectrum

nodes.summary: Expected number of blocks of size `i` when `k` blocks remain, for random joining started from `n` singletons: `k · C(n-i-1, k-2) / C(n-1, k-1)` (Fu 1995; Griffiths–Tavaré 1998). Equivalently, a given one of the `k` blocks has size `i` with probability `C(n-i-1, k-2) / C(n-1, k-1)`.
nodes.title: Expected number of blocks of size `i`

nodes.summary: The transition operator of random joining acting on a statistic `g` of block-size lists: the average of `g` over the lists obtained from `b` by merging a uniformly chosen pair of blocks (`g []` once fewer than two blocks remain). By `exists_finset_randomJoining`, its `j`-th iterate at `b` is the expectation of `g` at step `j` of random joining started from `b`.
nodes.title: Transition operator of random joining

nodes.summary: Merge the blocks at positions `i < j` of the block-size list `b`: remove both and append a block of size `b[i] + b[j]`.
nodes.title: Merging two blocks of a block-size list

nodes.summary: The random-joining law: `randomJoining m b ps` is the probability that `m` steps of random joining started from the block-size list `b` visit the list of block-size lists `ps` (starting with `b` itself). Each step merges a pair of blocks chosen uniformly among all pairs; the process stops once fewer than two blocks remain.
nodes.title: Random-joining law on block-size lists

nodes.summary: The total length of the branches subtending exactly `i` of the `n` sample copies, for the block-size history `ps` (entry `n - k` lists the block sizes while there are `k` lineages) and holding times `T`: `∑_{k=2}^{n} #{blocks of size i among k} · T k`.
nodes.title: Total branch length subtending i sample copies

nodes.summary: Summing the expected block counts against `E T_k = (k.choose 2)⁻¹` gives `2 / i`: `∑_{k=2}^{n} k C(n-i-1, k-2) / C(n-1, k-1) · (k.choose 2)⁻¹ = 2 / i` for `1 ≤ i < n`.
nodes.title: Expected block counts weighted by coalescence times sum to $2/i$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
